title: 1968 AHSME Problem 22
statement: A segment of length \(1\) is divided into four segments. Then there exists a quadrilateral with the four segments as sides if and only if each segment is:

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
equal to or greater than \(\dfrac18\) and less than
\(\dfrac12\)

solutions.text:
A simple nondegenerate quadrilateral exists exactly when each side is less than the sum of the other three. Since the total is \(1,\) this condition is \(s\lt1-s,\) or \(s\lt\frac{1}{2},\) for every segment.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: A nondegenerate quadrilateral exists exactly when the longest side is shorter than the other three combined
